findings.statement: The SGD 7,300 transfer went to a first-time payee. It greatly exceeded the prior observed maximum of SGD 194.28; the 19 baseline transactions were all card payments.
A new-device login at 00:00 UTC and a transfer-limit increase at 01:00 UTC preceded the transfer at 04:00 UTC, consistent with possible account takeover.

A SGD 127.11 domestic card payment occurred at the same recorded second as the transfer; ordinary spending does not explain away the transfer risk.

recommendedActions: Contact the customer through a trusted channel to verify the transfer, new device and limit change; secure the account and consider holding further transfers to the payee.
Urgently attempt recall of the SGD 7,300 and contact the receiving bank.
Investigate the embedded purported approval, preserve the event record and verify its provenance independently.

Review cooling-off enforcement and notification delivery for the new-device login and limit increase; assess whether the Shared Responsibility Framework applies and investigate any potential loss allocation.
Promptly assess and document whether to file a suspicious transaction report.

EUPG §4.7 and SRF §4.2.1 provide for at least a 12-hour cooling-off period during which high-risk activities cannot be performed after a protected-account login on a new device. Verify applicability and enforcement; the recorded limit increase was one hour after the login.

EUPG §4.9 and SRF §4.2.2 address real-time notification alerts for high-risk activities; SRF §4.2.2 also specifies alerts for a protected-account login on a new device. Verify delivery and applicability.
